• Lata occupies floor 2, flat A.
• Charu and Sana occupy flats with the same letter on different floors.
• Pia and Sana occupy flats with the same letter on different floors.
• The floor numbers of Charu and Sana differ by 2.
• Hema and Jaya occupy flats with different letters.
• Isha lives below Sana.
• Hema lives below Kiran.
• The floor numbers of Hema and Jaya differ by 1.
• The floor numbers of Hema and Isha differ by 1.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
savings access rural = su ni lu
savings credit growth = re ze ni
access credit digital = pa re lu
rural growth digital = su pa ze
savings access digital = ni pa lu
What is the code for “savings”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ni. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: savings = ni, access = lu, rural = su, credit = re, growth = ze, digital = pa.

questions.stem: In a queue of 35 candidates, a candidate is 15th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 18. New front rank = 15+3 = 18. Back rank = 35 − 18 + 1 = 18.

questions.stem: In a queue of 50 candidates, a candidate is 17th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. New front rank = 17+4 = 21. Back rank = 50 − 21 + 1 = 30.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 49 km west, turns right and walks 96 km, then turns right and walks 9 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 104. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 40 km along the initial direction and 96 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(40² + 96²) = 104 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 41 km west, turns left and walks 84 km, then turns left and walks 6 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 91. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 35 km along the initial direction and 84 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(35² + 84²) = 91 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 120 km south, turns right and walks 180 km, then turns right and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 204. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 96 km along the initial direction and 180 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(96² + 180²) = 204 km.

questions.stem: C is the brother of H. H is the mother of F. G is the father of C and H. How is C related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. C is the brother of F’s mother H. Therefore C is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: H is the only daughter of D. D is the father of H. G is the son of H. B is the sister of D. How is D related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of H, and H is G’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: D is the mother of F. B is the daughter of F. E is the father of F. How is B related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. E is a parent of F, and B is F’s daughter. Hence B is E’s grandchild.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹3200 each. One earns 25% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 6115.56. Recover each cost separately: 3200×100/125 + 3200×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 19 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 57. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+19)/(x+19) = 3/2 gives x = 19. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 220 m train moving at 90 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 10. Relative speed = (90 − 10.8) ×5/18 = 22 m/s. Time = 220/22.

questions.stem: The average weight of 29 people is 35 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 65. New total minus old total = (29+1)×(35+1) − 29×35 = 65.

questions.stem: A boat covers 170 km in still water in 10 hours. If the stream flows at 5 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 60. Still-water speed = 17 km/h. Upstream speed = 17 − 5. Distance = speed × 5.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹1800. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.

questions.stem: [Bar set] If the agricultural category at C increases by 20% and the business category there decreases by 10%, what is the new total?
questions.explanation: Answer: 2250. Derived data: A: first category 720, second category 480; B: first category 1360, second category 1020; C: first category 1200, second category 900; D: first category 560, second category 420; E: first category 960, second category 720. 1200 × 1.20 + 900 × 0.90.

questions.stem: [Bar set] If 25% of the business category at E is transferred to the agricultural category there, what is the new size of the agricultural category at E?
questions.explanation: Answer: 1140. Derived data: A: first category 720, second category 480; B: first category 1360, second category 1020; C: first category 1200, second category 900; D: first category 560, second category 420; E: first category 960, second category 720. New first category = 960 + 25% of 720.

questions.stem: [Bar set] The combined total at A and D is what percentage more or less than the total at C? Give the absolute percentage difference, rounded to two decimals.
questions.explanation: Answer: 3.81. Derived data: A: first category 720, second category 480; B: first category 1360, second category 1020; C: first category 1200, second category 900; D: first category 560, second category 420; E: first category 960, second category 720. Percentage difference = |total(A)+total(D)−total(C)| ÷ total(C) × 100.

questions.stem: [Bar set] What is the total number in the agricultural category at A and C together?
questions.explanation: Answer: 1920. Derived data: A: first category 720, second category 480; B: first category 1360, second category 1020; C: first category 1200, second category 900; D: first category 560, second category 420; E: first category 960, second category 720. 720 + 1200 = 1920.

questions.stem: A container holds 110 litres of pure milk. 22 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 70.4. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 110 × (4/5)².
